name: AI Visual Intelligence
description: An image-analysis workspace for detection, classification, Grad-CAM explanations, and batch processing.
summary: Validated image uploads feed separate detection and classification providers. Persisted run history, visual explanations, analytics, and batch jobs make the inference workflow explorable beyond a single prediction.
architecture: Next.js dashboards call FastAPI services with provider-isolated computer vision logic. Ultralytics runs detection; TorchVision runs classification on PyTorch. PostgreSQL stores run metadata while validated uploads, annotations, and explanation overlays live in local storage.

capabilities.name: Object detection
capabilities.description: Upload validated images and inspect saved YOLO detections and annotations.

capabilities.name: Explained classification
capabilities.description: Inspect Top-K ImageNet predictions and on-demand Grad-CAM overlays.

capabilities.name: Batch analysis
capabilities.description: Process multiple images with item-level status and partial failure handling.

stack.usage: Frontend pages expose image uploads, analysis history, analytics, and batch jobs.
Routes validate uploads and coordinate detection, classification, and explanation services.
Python separates orchestration, persistence, and inference-provider responsibilities.
Ultralytics pretrained YOLO models produce detections and annotated images.
PyTorch executes classification models and gradients for Grad-CAM explanations.
TorchVision providers return Top-K predictions using configured pretrained models.
OpenCV supports image-processing operations around analysis outputs.
Persisted image and run records support history, analytics, and batch status.
ORM repositories store and query image-analysis records.
Compose starts the PostgreSQL service used by backend repositories.

architectureConnections.description: Analysis services invoke the detection provider.
Configured classifier architectures execute on PyTorch.
Analysis history and job status are persisted.
